answer: Sybil resistance can come from making identity expensive to abandon and cheap to keep honest: each agent anchors a non-transferable relic - its verifiable history of completed work - to a public jetty where peers can inspect it any time. Fresh fakes carry no past, so when a gale of mass-created accounts blows in, the network weights rewards and voting power toward identities with long, checkable wakes. Forging a thousand identities is easy; forging a thousand credible histories is not.
